Reports indicate that Apple has significantly increased its vapor chamber orders, suggesting that this cooling technology is poised to play a more important role in future hardware product lines. Details are as follows.

Apple Doubles Down on Vapor Chamber Cooling Technology

Leaker "Fixed Focus Digital" posted on Weibo that Apple has "significantly increased its total vapor chamber order volume," speculating that this move "may be in preparation for stronger cooling solutions for its first foldable iPhone and the next-generation twentieth-anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro. This change helps address the heat issues that have persisted across several previous generations.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, then condensing it at a cooler location, dispersing the heat across a larger area before allowing the liquid to flow back and repeat the cycle.

You can watch the entire process in this fantastic video produced by Know Art below:

Although the Weibo post speculated that Apple's increased procurement this time is intended for the iPhone Ultra and the rumored twentieth-anniversary iPhone slated for release in 2027, judging by the timing, it would actually be more reasonable for this year's product lineup to adopt the technology first.

According to reports, Apple has asked suppliers to prepare approximately 10 million foldable iPhones, an increase from the earlier target of 7 to 8 million units. At the same time, it is also stockpiling around 70 million units of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. All three models are expected to feature vapor chamber cooling technology.

Amid the increase in orders, there are also reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and production yield issues, clearing obstacles to ramping up production ahead of the September launch.
